prompt:
You are an experienced sommelier comparing two wine recommenders. A
customer with no wine knowledge made this request:

"Can I get an unusual white wine that is sweet, smooth, and tastes like flowers and nuts? I want to give it to my boss, and it has to be something I have never heard of before."

List A:
Wine 1: Pinot Gris, US, $26. Tasting note: "Totally unusual and totally fun, this dark amber-colored wine is unexpected. It smells like flowers and honey, as if it will be sweet, but tastes dry and tangy, like blood oranges and raspberries. It's medium bodied and has a slight tannic or astringent finish, so it should pair well with toasted nut and cheeses."
Wine 2: White Blend, Austria, $41. Tasting note: "Sherry-like in style with nutty aromas and flavors, this is a curious but delicious wine. It's a white-wine blend with a touch of brandy flavor. As its name suggests, this is a fine apéritif."
Wine 3: Roussanne, US, $25. Tasting note: "The aroma of this uber-sophisticated white wine is almost like vintage Champagne, combining light smoky, toasted notes with a figgy, lees-stirred freshness. The plush and mature flavors resemble toasted walnuts, marzipan, white peach and honey, yet this is a dry dinner wine, not a dessert. It will make a great pairing with paté on toast or maybe a white truffle risotto."
Wine 4: Passerina, Italy, $19. Tasting note: "Here is a unique white wine with aromas of mature peach, honeydew melon and almond nut. It offers a compact, streamlined texture and medium persistency on the finish."
Wine 5: Sauvignon Blanc, US, $16. Tasting note: "This interesting and rather subtle wine smells like white pepper and pistachios and tastes like white peaches. It stays dry on the palate, while the texture spreads flavors smoothly for a sense of richness."

List B:
Wine 1: Chardonnay, US, $10. Tasting note: "This is a basic white wine with a few quirks. It smells floral and appley, and tastes quite dry and a bit sharp while carrying a candylike marshmallow note."
Wine 2: Fiano, US, $26. Tasting note: "This is an interesting, dry white wine from an unusual grape variety. It's more savory than fruity, as the aromas resemble white and black pepper, while flavors are subtle and figgy. The texture is quite rich and the finish lingers nicely. It's very full-bodied for a white, and definitely worth a try."
Wine 3: Marsanne, US, $12. Tasting note: "Here's a ripe, complex white wine with aromas and flavors ranging from tangerines, apricots and bananas to malted chocolate milk. It tastes very ripe and fruity, with a soft, creamy mouthfeel like peach syrup. There might be just a tad of residual sugar in there, but it's basically a dry wine."
Wine 4: Pinot Grigio, US, $10. Tasting note: "This is a sweet, softly simple wine whose apricot, citrus and peach flavors will satisfy those looking for a decent everyday white wine."
Wine 5: Sauvignon Blanc, US, $15. Tasting note: "This is an innocuous, flowery and lemony white wine priced to sell that offers a creamy texture amid a light body and soul. For picnics and larger gatherings, it'll represent well."

Which list answers the request better as a whole: relevance to every wish,
variety where the request leaves room, and fit for any occasion? If they
are equally good, say tie. Think briefly, then answer with JSON only:
{"reason": "<two sentences at most>", "better": "A" | "B" | "tie"}
